今天的主题：体育伦理、兴奋剂争议和公平竞赛。这组词对 G 类特别实用：写作 Task 2 讨论「运动员是否该被允许使用提高成绩药物」「体育要不要公平优先」时很常用；口语 Part 3 谈 sport、rules、cheating 也能直接用；阅读里遇到 doping、integrity、controversial 这类词也不陌生。

例句

  • Many people say doping destroys the integrity of sport.（很多人说服用兴奋剂破坏了体育的诚信。）
  • Allowing banned substances is a highly controversial idea.（允许使用违禁物质是一个极具争议的想法。）
  • Elite athletes should compete under the same rules.（精英运动员应该在同一套规则下比赛。）
  • Critics say the event will normalise cheating and set a bad example.（批评者说这项赛事会让作弊正常化，并树立坏榜样。）
  • It's fair to say the debate about fair play is far from over.（可以说，关于公平竞争的辩论远未结束。）

过关标准：遮住中文看英文，能说出 22 个以上的意思，再挑 5 个自己造句（试试用 doping、controversial、integrity 写一句你对体育公平的看法，Task 2 和口语 Part 3 都能直接用）。

BBC 6 Minute English：The Enhanced Games（增强运动会）。这集讲一场允许运动员在医疗监督下使用提高成绩药物的新赛事：有人说它更诚实、更安全，也有人说它越过道德底线、会让兴奋剂正常化。尼尔和皮帕讨论公平竞赛，并请出 BBC 体育编辑丹·罗恩谈这项「分裂性」赛事。主题正好对应 Task 2 观点文和口语 Part 3。音频和原文都已经放在页面里，不用打开 BBC 网站。

  1. 先把上面的听前生词过一遍，听不太懂可以先读懂原文再听。
  2. 第一遍不看文字，只听大意，回答开头的问题：兰斯·阿姆斯特朗在被抓之前赢过几次环法自行车赛？a) five b) six c) seven。顺便听出：增强运动会允许使用哪些药物？尼尔本人愿不愿意看这样的比赛？
  3. 第二遍点开下面的原文精听，听不出的地方暂停、倒回去并标出来。Asma Khalid 和 Dan Roan 两段是真实录音，语速稍快，多听几遍，尤其是 Dan Roan 讲 divisive、crosses an ethical line 和 normalising doping 那段。
  4. 第三遍挑 Neil 解释 cross the line / set a bad example 那段（"For the Games' critics, doping crosses an ethical line..."）跟读，模仿语调和连读。
  5. 记住 6 个表达：doping（服用兴奋剂）、it's fair to say（可以说）、divisive（引起分裂的）、cross the line（越界）、set a bad example（树立坏榜样）、normalise（使正常化）。
点开看原文（难词带中文，点虚线词显示）
💡 点击或悬停虚线词看中文；点击说话人名字可单独切换该段翻译

Neil：Hello, this is 6 Minute English from BBC Learning English. I'm Neil.

Neil：大家好，这里是 BBC 学习英语的《六分钟英语》。我是尼尔。

Pippa：And I'm Pippa. Sharing your Netflix password, lying about your age or not paying the bus fare are a few examples of cheating in daily life. But there's one place where cheating is usually considered wrong, and that's sport.

Pippa：我是皮帕。把 Netflix 密码分享给别人、谎报年龄、或者不买公交车票，这些都是日常生活里作弊的例子。但有一个地方，作弊通常被认为是不对的，那就是体育。

Neil：Cheating in sport through the use of performance-enhancing drugs提高成绩的药物, informally called doping服用兴奋剂（违禁药物）, is normally considered wrong. Just ask American cycling legend自行车传奇 Lance Armstrong, who was thrown out of被逐出 the sport for using banned substances违禁物质. But earlier this year, a sporting event took place which turned the debate把争论颠倒／彻底改变了争论 about drugs in sport upside down颠倒过来. Here's Asma Khalid from BBC World Service's The Global Story to explain:

Neil：在体育里用提高成绩的药物作弊——俗称 doping（服用兴奋剂）——通常被认为是不对的。问问美国自行车传奇兰斯·阿姆斯特朗就知道了，他因为使用违禁物质被逐出这项运动。但今年早些时候，一场体育赛事把关于体育用药的争论彻底颠倒了过来。下面请 BBC 世界服务节目《全球故事》的阿斯玛·哈立德来解释：

Asma Khalid：This weekend, elite精英的 athletes运动员 from around the world are descending on涌向 Las Vegas, Nevada, for the first-of-its-kind前所未有的，首创的 sporting competition known as The Enhanced Games. It's kind of like the Olympics, but only for swimming, sprinting短跑 and weightlifting举重. The aim is to break world records. In fact, some of these competitors are former Olympians – medallists奖牌得主 battling it out一决高下 for money and glory金钱和荣耀. But there's one big difference...

Asma Khalid：这个周末，来自世界各地的精英运动员正涌向内华达州的拉斯维加斯，参加一场前所未有的体育比赛——增强运动会（The Enhanced Games）。它有点像奥运会，但只比游泳、短跑和举重。目标是打破世界纪录。事实上，有些参赛者是前奥运选手——奖牌得主们为了金钱和荣耀一决高下。但有一个很大的不同……

Pippa：The big difference is that The Enhanced Games allow athletes运动员 to use performance-enhancing drugs提高成绩的药物 that are banned in professional sports. In these games, nicknamed The Doping Olympics兴奋剂奥运会, steroids类固醇, growth hormones生长激素 and stimulants兴奋剂，刺激物 are all OK. You're a big sports fan, Neil. Would you enjoy watching a sport where the athletes运动员 have taken drugs?

Pippa：最大的不同是，增强运动会允许运动员使用在职业体育中被禁的提高成绩药物。在这些绰号叫「兴奋剂奥运会」的比赛里，类固醇、生长激素和兴奋剂都可以用。尼尔，你是个铁杆体育迷。你会喜欢看运动员吃过药的比赛吗？

Neil：No, I wouldn't. I really don't think that's fair. I think we need to know that all the athletes运动员 start and compete from the same level.

Neil：不，我不会。我真的觉得那样不公平。我觉得我们需要知道，所有运动员都是从同一起跑线出发、在同一水平上比赛的。

Pippa：Yeah, I guess that makes sense. I don't really watch that many sports so I guess I wouldn't notice the difference, but if you're really into sport you care about the rules, right?

Pippa：嗯，我觉得有道理。我其实不怎么看比赛，所以大概不会注意到差别，但如果你真的很热爱体育，你就会在乎规则，对吧？

Neil：Yes, absolutely. And in this episode we'll dive into the controversial有争议的 world of The Enhanced Games, learning some useful new words and phrases along the way. And remember, you'll find all the vocabulary, plus a quiz and a worksheet练习题, on our website, bbclearningenglish.com.

Neil：对，完全正确。这一期我们会深入探讨增强运动会这个有争议的世界，一路学一些有用的新词和新短语。记住，所有词汇，还有小测验和练习题，都可以在我们的网站 bbclearningenglish.com 找到。

Pippa：But now I have a question for you, Neil. You mentioned the famous sporting cheat Lance Armstrong, but how many times did Lance Armstrong win the famous race, the Tour de France环法自行车赛, before he was finally caught out被抓到，被揭穿? Was it:
a) five,
b) six, or
c) seven?

Pippa：不过先问你一个问题，尼尔。你提到了著名的体育作弊者兰斯·阿姆斯特朗，那么在他最终被抓之前，兰斯·阿姆斯特朗赢过几次著名的环法自行车赛？是：a）五次，b）六次，还是 c）七次？

Neil：Ooh... Well, it was a lot, so I think I'll go for
c) seven.

Neil：哦……反正很多，所以我选 c）七次。

Pippa：Well, we'll find out the answer at the end of the programme. Now, it's no exaggeration毫不夸张 to say that The Enhanced Games are controversial有争议的. After all, organisations like the World Anti-Doping Agency世界反兴奋剂机构 have spent decades fighting performance-enhancing drugs提高成绩的药物 in sport. Here's BBC sports editor Dan Roan on World Service programme The Global Story.

Pippa：好，节目最后会揭晓答案。现在可以说，毫不夸张地说，增强运动会是有争议的。毕竟，像世界反兴奋剂机构这样的组织已经花了几十年时间打击体育中的提高成绩药物。下面是 BBC 体育编辑丹·罗恩在世界服务节目《全球故事》里的说法。

Dan Roan：I think it's fair to say可以说（引出公允说法） it's one of the most divisive引起分裂／分歧的 and controversial有争议的 events that the world of sport has seen for a long time. It's an event where performance-enhancing drugs提高成绩的药物, banned elsewhere in mainstream sport of course, are actually allowed to be taken by the competitors under medical supervision医疗监督.

Dan Roan：我觉得可以说，这是体育界很长时间以来见过的最分裂、最有争议的赛事之一。在这项赛事里，提高成绩的药物——当然在主流体育的其他地方是被禁的——实际上被允许在医疗监督下由参赛者服用。

Neil：Dan Roan says, "It's fair to say可以说（引出公允说法） The Enhanced Games are controversial有争议的." He uses the phrase it's fair to say可以说（引出公允说法） to introduce a statement that he considers to be balanced and reasonable – that the games are controversial有争议的.

Neil：丹·罗恩说：「可以说增强运动会是有争议的。」他用短语 it's fair to say 来引出一个他认为公允、合理的说法——也就是说这些运动会是有争议的。

Pippa：Dan also describes the games as divisive引起分裂／分歧的 – an adjective that means causing a lot of disagreement between people. Much of this disagreement is about the use of performance-enhancing drugs提高成绩的药物 themselves. The Games' organisers point out that all drugs are approved批准 by the US Food and Drug Agency and taken openly under medical supervision医疗监督, which they say makes them safer than when they are taken secretly秘密地 at competitions elsewhere. But there are many critics批评者 too, as Dan Roan outlined to BBC World Service's The Global Story.

Pippa：丹还用 divisive 来形容这些运动会——这个形容词的意思是在人们之间引起很多分歧。这些分歧很大程度上是关于使用提高成绩药物本身。运动会组织者指出，所有药物都经美国食品药品管理局批准，并且在医疗监督下公开服用，他们说这比在其他比赛里偷偷服用更安全。但也有很多批评者，正如丹·罗恩向 BBC 世界服务节目《全球故事》所概述的。

Dan Roan：But the critics批评者, of course, say that this crosses an ethical line越过道德底线, that it sets a dreadful example树立糟糕的榜样 because it risks normalising使正常化 doping服用兴奋剂（违禁药物）. It could harm the integrity诚信，正直, therefore, of sport, and it could be dangerous to the health of those taking part.

Dan Roan：但批评者当然会说，这越过了道德底线，树立了一个糟糕的榜样，因为它有可能让服用兴奋剂变得正常化。因此，它可能会损害体育的诚信，也可能危及参赛者的健康。

Neil：For the Games' critics批评者, doping服用兴奋剂（违禁药物） crosses an ethical line越过道德底线. The phrase to cross the line越界，做出不可接受的事 means to start behaving in a way that's not socially acceptable. These critics批评者 say the Games set a bad example树立坏榜样, meaning that they encourage others to behave badly as well. Why is that, Pippa?

Neil：对运动会的批评者来说，服用兴奋剂越过了道德底线。短语 to cross the line 的意思是开始做出社会上不能接受的行为。这些批评者说，运动会 set a bad example，意思是它们鼓励别人也做出不好的行为。为什么会这样，皮帕？

Pippa：Well, it's because critics批评者 argue the games normalise使正常化 the use of performance drugs in sport. If you normalise使正常化 something, you treat it as normal or acceptable when previously以前 it wasn't. But with arguments strongly held on both sides, the debate is far from over远未结束. So Neil, have you changed your opinion after hearing both sides of the story事情的两面?

Pippa：因为批评者认为，这些运动会让体育中使用提高成绩药物变得正常化。如果你 normalise 某件事，就是把它当作正常或可接受的，而以前并不是这样。但双方论点都很强硬，这场辩论远未结束。那么尼尔，听完双方的说法，你改变看法了吗？

Neil：No, I haven't. I think it's just not fair, and I think if you're not fair in sport, what's the point?

Neil：没有。我觉得就是不公平，而且我觉得如果体育里都不公平了，那还有什么意义？

Pippa：Well, let's hear the answer to my quiz question, Neil. I asked you how many times Lance Armstrong won the Tour de France环法自行车赛, and it was
c) seven times, consecutively连续地 between 1999 and 2005. Of course, we now know that there were performance-enhancing drugs提高成绩的药物 involved.

Pippa：好，我们来听我那个测验问题的答案，尼尔。我问你兰斯·阿姆斯特朗赢过几次环法，答案是 c）七次，从 1999 年到 2005 年连续夺冠。当然，我们现在知道其中涉及了提高成绩的药物。

Neil：OK. So, now it's time to recap回顾 the vocabulary we've learned, starting with doping服用兴奋剂（违禁药物） – using banned drugs to perform better in sporting competitions.

Neil：好。现在该回顾我们学过的词汇了，先从 doping 开始——使用违禁药物来在体育比赛中表现得更好。

Pippa：You can use the phrase it's fair to say可以说（引出公允说法） to introduce a statement you consider to be balanced, reasonable or true.

Pippa：你可以用短语 it's fair to say 来引出一个你认为公允、合理或真实的说法。

Neil：If something is divisive引起分裂／分歧的, it causes disagreement between people.

Neil：如果某件事是 divisive，它就会在人们之间引起分歧。

Pippa：The idiom cross the line越界，做出不可接受的事 means to start behaving in an unacceptable way.

Pippa：习语 cross the line 的意思是开始做出不可接受的行为。

Neil：If you set a bad example树立坏榜样, you behave in a way that encourages others to behave badly.

Neil：如果你 set a bad example，就是用自己的行为鼓励别人也表现得很差。

Pippa：And finally, to normalise使正常化 something means to treat it as normal or acceptable when previously以前 it wasn't.

Pippa：最后，to normalise something 的意思是把某事当作正常或可接受的，而以前并不是这样。

Neil：OK. Once again, our six minutes are up, but if you'd like to practise more, you'll find a quiz and worksheet练习题 on our website, bbclearningenglish.com. See you again soon. But for now, it's goodbye.

Neil：好。我们的六分钟又到了，但如果你想多练习，可以在我们的网站 bbclearningenglish.com 找到小测验和练习题。很快再见。现在先说再见。

Pippa：Bye!

Pippa：再见！

过关标准：不看原文能用中文说出这集讲了什么（增强运动会是什么、为什么有争议、批评者担心什么、尼尔的态度），6 个表达都知道意思，Neil 那段能流利读下来。

小练习

  1. Using banned drugs to perform better is called ______.（服用兴奋剂）
  2. It's ______ to say the Enhanced Games are controversial.（可以说）
  3. The event is highly ______ — people strongly disagree about it.（引起分裂的）
  4. Critics say doping ______ the line of what is ethically acceptable.（越过）
  5. If stars cheat, they may set a bad ______ for young athletes.（榜样）
  6. Some people worry the games will ______ doping in sport.（使正常化）
点开看答案

开头那题选 c，seven。兰斯·阿姆斯特朗在 1999 到 2005 年连续七次夺得环法，后来被证实使用了提高成绩药物。尼尔猜对了。增强运动会允许类固醇、生长激素和兴奋剂等；尼尔本人不愿意看，因为觉得不公平。填空：1. doping 2. fair 3. divisive 4. crosses / crossed 5. example 6. normalise

今天的小思考（为口语 Part 3 和大作文做准备）：Should athletes be allowed to use performance-enhancing drugs under medical supervision? 用英语说两三句：I don't think it's fair because ... / Some people argue that ..., but I believe ...。也可以想想：如果所有人都用药，世界纪录还有意义吗？
